name: gate
wording: A point at a handover where the work stops for the operator's sign-off: a story's read-back, held by the architect; a story's plan read-back, held by the lead, which a task with no story skips unless the operator calls it; a pull request the operator reviews, held by the lead before it merges; release; a fork that is irreversible, about value or beyond the architect's competence; and any point the operator calls, stop included. A gate is held in the session of the party whose handover it is, which ends its turn there, its reply ending with the sign-off it waits on, until the operator answers; the operator joins that session, and the party that delegated the work learns only that it waits on the operator, and then the result. Pushing a branch or opening a pull request is never a gate, and between gates the agents work without checking in.
reason: Divided authority needs the points where the operator's sign-off is due to be named, held by the party whose handover it is, and nowhere else, so agents neither run past them nor check in between them; a gate is the point, kept apart from the sign-off exercised there.
